title: MATH GAOKAO - 326
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.concept: Mean from a Discrete Frequency Table
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the arithmetic mean from a discrete frequency table.
questions.question:
The frequency table below gives values of \(x\) and their frequencies \(f\). Find the mean of the data.
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
x & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 \\
\hline
f & 2 & 3 & 5 & 4 & 1
\end{array}
\]
questions.hint: Multiply each value by its frequency, add these products, and divide by the total frequency.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the median of a discrete data set given by a frequency table.
questions.question:
The frequency table below gives a data set. Find its median.
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
x & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 \\
\hline
f & 4 & 5 & 6 & 3 & 2
\end{array}
\]
questions.explanation: The total frequency is \(4+5+6+3+2=20\). The median is the average of the 10th and 11th ordered values. The cumulative frequencies are \(4,9,15,18,20\). Since the 10th and 11th values both lie in the group \(x=3\), the median is \(3\).
questions.hint: Use cumulative frequencies to locate the middle position or positions in the ordered data.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the mode from a frequency table.
questions.question:
The frequency table below shows the values and their frequencies. What is the mode?
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
x & 10 & 11 & 12 & 13 & 14 \\
\hline
f & 5 & 8 & 12 & 7 & 3
\end{array}
\]
questions.explanation: The mode is the value with the greatest frequency. The largest frequency is \(12\), which corresponds to the value \(x=12\). Therefore, the mode is \(12\).
questions.hint: Find the value whose frequency is the largest in the table.

questions.learningObjective: Find an unknown frequency using the total number of observations.
questions.question:
The frequency table below has a total frequency of \(30\). Find the value of \(k\).
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\
\hline
f & 5 & 8 & k & 6 & 3
\end{array}
\]
questions.explanation:
The sum of all frequencies must equal \(30\):
\[
5+8+k+6+3=30.
\]
So \(22+k=30\), which gives \(k=8\).
questions.hint: Add all frequencies, set the sum equal to the total frequency, and solve for the unknown.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the mean of data presented in a frequency table.
questions.question:
Using the frequency table below, calculate the mean.
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
x & 2 & 4 & 6 & 8 \\
\hline
f & 3 & 5 & 4 & 2
\end{array}
\]
questions.explanation:
The total frequency is \(3+5+4+2=14\). The sum of \(xf\) is
\[
2(3)+4(5)+6(4)+8(2)=6+20+24+16=66.
\]
Therefore, the mean is \(\frac{66}{14}=\frac{33}{7}\).
questions.hint: Compute \(\sum xf\) and divide it by \(\sum f\).

questions.concept: Frequency from a Cumulative Frequency Table
questions.learningObjective: Determine the frequency of an interval from cumulative frequencies.
questions.question:
The cumulative frequency table below gives the number of observations less than each upper bound. How many observations lie in the interval \(20 \le x < 30\)?
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
\text{Interval} & x<10 & x<20 & x<30 & x<40 \\
\hline
\text{Cumulative frequency} & 5 & 12 & 20 & 25
\end{array}
\]
questions.explanation:
The number of observations less than \(30\) is \(20\), and the number less than \(20\) is \(12\). Therefore, the number in \(20 \le x < 30\) is
\[
20-12=8.
\]
questions.hint: The frequency of an interval is found by subtracting consecutive cumulative frequencies.

questions.concept: Median Class of a Grouped Frequency Table
questions.learningObjective: Identify the median class from a grouped frequency table.
questions.question:
The grouped frequency table below gives the distribution of a data set. Which class contains the median?
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
\text{Class} & 0\text{--}10 & 10\text{--}20 & 20\text{--}30 & 30\text{--}40 & 40\text{--}50 \\
\hline
f & 4 & 6 & 10 & 8 & 2
\end{array}
\]
questions.explanation: The total frequency is \(4+6+10+8+2=30\), so the median position is between the 15th and 16th observations. The cumulative frequencies are \(4,10,20,28,30\). The 15th and 16th observations both fall in the class \(20\text{--}30\). Hence, the median class is \(20\text{--}30\).
questions.hint: Find the class containing the \(\frac{n}{2}\)-th observation by using cumulative frequencies.

questions.concept: Modal Class of a Grouped Frequency Table
questions.learningObjective: Identify the modal class from a grouped frequency table.
questions.question:
The grouped frequency table below shows the distribution of a data set. What is the modal class?
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
\text{Class} & 0\text{--}5 & 5\text{--}10 & 10\text{--}15 & 15\text{--}20 & 20\text{--}25 \\
\hline
f & 3 & 7 & 12 & 9 & 4
\end{array}
\]
questions.explanation: The modal class is the class with the largest frequency. The frequencies are \(3,7,12,9,4\), so the largest frequency is \(12\), corresponding to the class \(10\text{--}15\).
questions.hint: Compare the frequencies and select the class with the greatest frequency.

questions.concept: Mean from a Grouped Frequency Table
questions.learningObjective: Estimate the mean of grouped data using class midpoints.
questions.question:
Estimate the mean of the grouped data below by using class midpoints.
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
\text{Class} & 0\text{--}10 & 10\text{--}20 & 20\text{--}30 & 30\text{--}40 \\
\hline
f & 5 & 8 & 10 & 7
\end{array}
\]
questions.explanation:
The class midpoints are \(5,15,25,35\). The total frequency is \(5+8+10+7=30\). The sum of midpoint times frequency is
\[
5(5)+15(8)+25(10)+35(7)=25+120+250+245=640.
\]
Thus the estimated mean is
\[
\frac{640}{30}=\frac{64}{3}.
\]
questions.hint: Replace each class by its midpoint, then compute \(\frac{\sum fm}{\sum f}\).

questions.concept: Missing Frequency from a Given Mean
questions.learningObjective: Determine an unknown frequency using a given mean of a frequency table.
questions.question:
The frequency table below has mean \(3\). Find the value of \(a\).
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
x & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 \\
\hline
f & 2 & a & 5 & 4 & 1
\end{array}
\]
questions.hint: Write the mean condition as \(\frac{\sum xf}{\sum f}=3\), then solve the resulting equation for \(a\).
